why_this_is_not_post_hoc.concern: Promoting an arm chosen from exploratory data can be a rule fitted to a result. Worse than a screen winner: this candidate was located (R12) and measured (R14) before any promotion rule existed.
why_this_is_not_post_hoc.what_was_post_hoc: The CANDIDATE. The 8-15 cut was chosen after reading RCWM-T1 R12 (weight-spliced hybrids on 640 pilot one-step items; the hybrid grid {12,16,20,24} was fixed before R12, the choice of 8-15 was not) and R14 (D-23: arms loc8_15 and up16_27 on 248 off-task prompts and pilot chained decisions). R12's prefix cuts: 8-11 LO/HI/MID; 8-15 0.85/1.00/0.97 HI; 8-19 0.96/1.00/1.01 HI; 8-23 0.92/1.00/1.00 HI. 8-15 was chosen, implicitly and without a written criterion, as the smallest cut that is HI in every family (minimising the retained delta); of the three HI prefix cuts it has the lowest ledger FR. The 248 prompts were declared at birth 'no training or selection'; D-26 went beyond that declaration. The registration forbids further forks (no other cut screened); it does not undo this one.
why_this_is_not_post_hoc.answer: The DECISION is not post hoc. PREREG-L1's rule was frozen (evidence/PREREG_L1_FREEZE.json, {{freeze_sha256}}) before any of its instruments was read for this core, every run invocation was bound to that freeze, the decisive endpoints use only instruments that played no part in choosing the cut, the bytes were fixed in advance (sha256 6282b456..., L8_15_EXPECTED.json), no other cut was screened, and no threshold was adjusted after results were read. SPARSE-001's sentence 'the rule was fixed before any arm was built' is NOT claimed here: it would be false.

why_this_is_not_post_hoc.instruments_separation_evidence: SELECT-VIEWS-001 shares 0 of 15,629 (before, event) payloads with the RCWM pilot bank; the 456 drift prompts exclude every id, template family and text of the 248 and every id and user text of the HSKILL-002 source pools (hence both HSKILL-002 banks, the reserved CONFIRM bank never opened); RCWM never read the arithmetic panel.
